To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rate of exogenous release of insulin is controlled by the threshold of glucose concentration and that the intermittent supply of insulin is more efficient than constant supply in producing a sustained glucose response in type 1 diabetic patients.
the intermittent insulin supply is more efficient in producing the physiological response than a continuous supply.
the dual wave boluses technique can reduce the time needed to reach the physiological range and that oscillatory insulin supply is more efficient in controlling glucose concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the insulin release profile on the regulation of blood glucose concentration in type I diabetes.
the design of a mathematical model that can be used for the development of a closed-loop insulin delivery system.
the design of optimal insulin release profile for the dual wave technique, and with the analysis of oscillatory dynamics in the model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CSII is an effective treatment for diabetes and that it is a good alternative to multiple daily insulin injections.
the intermittent insulin release, as a function time, is a more effective strategy than a constant insulin infusion in the control of glucose levels in type 1 diabetic patients.
the optimal profile of the insulin supply should be determined by the characteristics (e.g., TDD, body size, etc.) of the individual patient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model provides an efficient method of predicting the optimal profile for insulin supply, which can be used as a guideline in the clinical management of type 1 diabetes.
the optimal control of glucose concentration is a result of a complex interplay between the insulin supply and the characteristics of the body.
the dual wave bolous technique is more efficient in controlling blood glucose level than the constant insulin supply, and that an oscillatory release of insulin will further enhance the efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of insulin release should be modulated in order to maintain a physiological level of glucose concentration in CSII.
the rate of glucose metabolism is the key determinant of the rate of glucose clearance from the blood.
the optimal profile of an insulin supply can be determined by using mathematical models to simulate a patient's response to a specific insulin release rate.
